121: Hill continues from the previous chapter's conclusion, emphasizing that riches in huge quantities are never the result of HARD work alone—they come in response to definite demands based on definite principles, not chance or luck. He defines an idea as an impulse of thought that impels action by appealing to the imagination. Master salespeople know ideas can be sold where merchandise cannot; ordinary salespeople don't know this. He shares the story of a book publisher who discovered many people buy titles, not contents—by merely changing a non-selling book's title, sales jumped over a million copies without changing the inside. That simple act was IMAGINATION at work. There is no standard price on ideas; creators make their own price. The movie industry created millionaires who couldn't create ideas but had imagination to recognize them. Great fortunes start when a creator of ideas and a seller of ideas work in harmony. Carnegie surrounded himself with people who could do what he couldn't. Hill notes millions hope for favorable breaks, but the safest plan is not depending on luck. His biggest opportunity came from meeting Andrew Carnegie, but 25 years of determined effort were required before it became an asset.
122: Hill reflects on his own journey: the favorable break was meeting Carnegie, who planted the idea of organizing achievement principles into a philosophy of success. But the DETERMINATION, DEFINITENESS OF PURPOSE, DESIRE, and PERSISTENT EFFORT of 25 years were extraordinary. It was no ordinary DESIRE that survived disappointment, discouragement, temporary defeat, criticism, and constant reminders of 'waste of time'—it was a BURNING DESIRE, an OBSESSION. When Carnegie first planted the idea, Hill coaxed, nursed, and enticed it to remain alive. Gradually, the idea became a giant under its own power and coaxed, nursed, and drove him. Ideas are like that: first you give life and action to ideas, then they take on power and sweep aside all opposition. Ideas are intangible forces with more power than the physical brains that birth them. They live on after the brain that created them returns to dust. Christianity began with a simple idea—'Do unto others as you would have others do unto you.' Christ has gone, but His IDEA marches on. Someday it may fulfill Christ's deepest DESIRE. The IDEA has been developing only two thousand years—give it time!
123: This page features two inspirational quotes in large text. The first repeats the principle: 'Riches, when they come in huge quantities, are never the result of HARD work! Riches come, if they come at all, in response to definite demands, based upon the application of definite principles, and not by chance or luck.' The second states: 'SUCCESS REQUIRES NO APOLOGIES. FAILURE PERMITS NO ALIBIS.' These quotes serve as a thematic divider between Chapter 5 (Imagination) and Chapter 6 (Organized Planning), encapsulating core principles: that wealth follows the application of definite principles rather than luck or labor alone, and that success stands on its own merit while failure offers no valid excuses. The page bears the OceanofPDF.com watermark.
124: This page opens Chapter 6: ORGANIZED PLANNING—The Crystallization of Desire Into Action (The Sixth Step to Riches). Hill recalls that everything worthwhile begins as DESIRE, and the first step from abstract to concrete is into IMAGINATION's workshop where PLANS are created. He instructs readers on building practical plans: (a) Ally yourself with a group of as many people as needed to create and carry out plans, using the Master Mind Principle (Chapter 9)—this is absolutely essential. (b) Before forming the Master Mind Alliance, decide what advantages and benefits you offer members in return—no one works indefinitely without compensation, though not always monetary. (c) Arrange to meet with members at least twice weekly until plans are perfected. (d) Maintain PERFECT HARMONY between yourself and every member—without it, the Master Mind Principle cannot function and failure follows.
125: Hill emphasizes two key facts: first, this undertaking is of major importance, so plans must be faultless. Second, you need the advantage of others' experience, education, native ability, and imagination—this matches the methods of all who accumulated great fortunes. No individual has sufficient experience alone to ensure great fortune without cooperation. Every plan should be the joint creation of yourself and your Master Mind Group. If the first plan fails, replace it with a new one, and keep replacing until you find one that WORKS. This is where most people fail—lack of PERSISTENCE in creating new plans. The most intelligent person cannot succeed without practical, workable plans. Temporary defeat is not permanent failure—it may only mean plans were unsound. Build other plans and start over. Edison 'failed' 10,000 times before perfecting the incandescent bulb. Millions live in misery and poverty because they lack a sound plan for accumulating a fortune.
126: Hill cites Henry Ford as accumulating a fortune not through superior mind but by adopting and following a sound PLAN. A thousand people with better education than Ford live in poverty because they lack the RIGHT plan. Achievement can be no greater than plans are sound. No one is whipped until they QUIT—in their own mind. James J. Hill met temporary defeat raising capital for his transcontinental railroad but turned defeat into victory through new plans. Ford met temporary defeat at the beginning and after reaching near the top, but created new plans and marched on. We see people's triumphs but overlook their temporary defeats. NO FOLLOWER OF THIS PHILOSOPHY can expect to accumulate a fortune without experiencing temporary defeat. When defeat comes, accept it as a signal that plans are unsound, rebuild, and set sail again. 'A QUITTER NEVER WINS—AND A WINNER NEVER QUITS.' When selecting Master Mind members, choose those who don't take defeat seriously. Hill dispels the belief that only MONEY can make money—DESIRE transmuted into monetary equivalent is the agency through which money is made. Money is inert matter that can 'hear' when a person who DESIRES it calls it to come. He then introduces 'Planning the Sale of Services.'
127: Hill states the remainder of Chapter 6 covers marketing personal services—practical help for anyone with services to market, and priceless for those aspiring to leadership. Intelligent planning is essential for success. He notes practically all great fortunes began as compensation for personal services or sale of IDEAS. There are two types of people: LEADERS and FOLLOWERS. Decide early which you intend to be—the difference in compensation is vast. It's no disgrace to be a follower, but no credit to remain one. Most great leaders began as INTELLIGENT FOLLOWERS, acquiring knowledge from their leaders. Hill then presents 'The 11 Major Factors of Leadership': (1) UNWAVERING COURAGE based on self-knowledge. (2) SELF-CONTROL—cannot control others without it. (3) A KEEN SENSE OF JUSTICE. (4) DEFINITENESS OF DECISION—waverers cannot lead. (5) DEFINITENESS OF PLANS—leaders must plan their work and work their plan.
128: The 11 Major Factors of Leadership continue: (6) THE HABIT OF DOING MORE THAN PAID FOR—leaders must do more than they require of followers. (7) A PLEASING PERSONALITY—leadership calls for respect. (8) SYMPATHY AND UNDERSTANDING—must understand followers and their problems. (9) MASTERY OF DETAIL. (10) WILLINGNESS TO ASSUME FULL RESPONSIBILITY—leaders must accept responsibility for followers' mistakes and shortcomings. (11) COOPERATION—must understand and apply cooperative effort. Hill identifies two forms of leadership: LEADERSHIP BY CONSENT (with followers' sympathy, most effective) and LEADERSHIP BY FORCE (without consent). History proves Leadership by Force cannot endure—dictators and kings fall. The world has entered a new era requiring new leaders and a new brand of leadership in business and industry. Old-school Force leaders must acquire understanding of cooperation or be relegated to followers. The future employer-employee relationship will be mutual cooperation based on equitable profit division, more like partnership. Napoleon, Kaiser Wilhelm, the Czar of Russia, and the King of Spain exemplified leadership by force—their leadership passed. Leadership by Consent is the only enduring brand.
129: Hill states the new brand of LEADERSHIP will embrace the 11 Major Factors plus others. Those who make these the basis of leadership will find abundant opportunity. Difficult economic times were prolonged largely because the world lacked this new brand of leadership. The demand now exceeds the supply—this necessity may be the reader's OPPORTUNITY. He then presents 'The 10 Major Causes of Failure in Leadership': (1) INABILITY TO ORGANIZE DETAILS—genuine leaders are never 'too busy.' (2) UNWILLINGNESS TO RENDER HUMBLE SERVICE—'The greatest among ye shall be the servant of all.' (3) EXPECTATION OF PAY FOR WHAT THEY KNOW INSTEAD OF WHAT THEY DO—the world pays for what you DO or induce others to do. (4) FEAR OF COMPETITION FROM FOLLOWERS—able leaders train understudies; people receive more pay for ability to get others to perform. (5) LACK OF IMAGINATION—without it, leaders cannot meet emergencies or create plans. (6) SELFISHNESS—leaders who claim all honor breed resentment; great leaders claim none. (7) INTEMPERANCE—destroys endurance and vitality. (8) DISLOYALTY—perhaps should head the list; disloyal leaders cannot long maintain leadership. (9) OVEREMPHASIS ON AUTHORITY—real leaders lead by encouragement, not fear. (10) OVEREMPHASIS ON TITLE—competent leaders need no title; those who emphasize title generally have little else.
130: Hill calls these the more common causes of leadership failure—any one fault is sufficient to induce failure. He then identifies 'Some Fertile Fields in Which New Leadership Will Be Required': First, POLITICS—most politicians have become legalized racketeers, increasing taxes and debauching industry. Second, BANKING—leaders have lost public confidence and begun reform. Third, INDUSTRY—old-type leaders thought in terms of dividends, not human equations; future leaders must regard themselves as quasi-public officials, as exploitation of workers is past. Fourth, RELIGION—leaders must give more attention to followers' temporal needs and current problems. Fifth, PROFESSIONS (law, medicine, education)—especially education, which must teach HOW TO APPLY knowledge, dealing more with PRACTICE and less with THEORY. Sixth, JOURNALISM—newspapers must divorce from special privilege and advertising subsidy, ceasing to be propaganda organs. These fields offer abundant opportunity for new leaders as the world undergoes rapid change.
